title: Centralise gateway policy in the dispatcher: deny-first LOCKED allowlist table, NsPtr typestate on every handler, sentinel-gate the pin-attempt-log handler, count unknown CMDs as anomalies
threat: PIN gating and pointer validation are discipline-enforced per handler (20 `pin_verified` reads across 15 cmd_* files; the `NsPtr<T>` typestate adopted by one veneer), so a new command (e.g. USB-05, OFFCHAIN_SYNC, the 2026-09 pin-attempt log) can and did land without the uniform FI shape: `cmd_pin_attempt_log.rs:23` is a production, PIN-less handler with a bare `if !validate_ns_write_ptr` — the FAIL-OUT shape HIGH-1 removed elsewhere; a single branch-skip writes 23 bytes into secure SRAM. Unknown CMDs return a soft InternalError with no counting, so a host can probe the dispatcher indefinitely.
proposal: (1) In `dispatch`/the veneers: a single `const LOCKED_OK: &[u32] = &[CMD_GET_REMAINING, CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK, CMD_IS_UNLOCKED, CMD_GET_PIN_ATTEMPT_LOG(pending #719)]` checked deny-first through the FI sentinel before the match; handlers keep their own check as belt-and-braces but the table is the reviewed policy (mirrors Trezor ALLOW_WHILE_LOCKED). (2) Migrate every cmd_* to `NsPtr::<T>::new(addr).validate_read/write(len)` so pointer validation is type-enforced; delete the free functions once no caller remains and add a semgrep rule forbidding `validate_ns_*_ptr(` outside ns_ptr.rs. (3) Fix cmd_pin_attempt_log to `check_true_into_sentinel` + HandlerGuard and track it (untracked today; #140 covers prodtest only and still says 12 gates — now 15). (4) Unknown/forbidden CMD increments an S-SRAM anomaly counter; above N (e.g. 8 per unlock session) the device locks (zeroize, not wipe) and the reason is logged to the pin-attempt ring.
rationale: Ledger's LSB-023 root cause was per-app guards decaying; Trezor's wire layer applies deny-first filters centrally and treats an invalid smcall/syscall as fatal. pq1's threat-model.md:263 already describes the typestate as THE mechanism — making the docs true is cheaper than keeping the drift.
repo_evidence: grep -c pin_verified|is_unlocked() secure/src/nsc/cmd_*.rs -> 20 sites in 15 of 20 handler files
grep -rl NsPtr secure/src -> only nsc/ns_ptr.rs, nsc/mod.rs, nsc_core_under_test/pure_tests.rs
docs/security/threat-model.md:263 (claims NsPtr validates every gateway pointer — drift)
GitHub #140 OPEN (prodtest bare gates), #719 OPEN (pin-log disclosure decision)
vendor_precedent: Trezor message_handler.py:95-183 + lock_manager.py (ALLOW_WHILE_LOCKED deny-first filter), smcall_dispatch.c:475-488 (fatal on invalid smcall), smcall_verifiers.c (every smcall has a `__verified` probe wrapper).
risks: Lock-on-N-unknown-CMDs is a host-triggerable DoS of an unlocked session (acceptable: re-PIN) — keep N generous and never escalate to the SE wipe; the NsPtr migration touches every handler and needs the QEMU e2e + Kani pure-tests re-run; the #719 decision must be taken before the table is frozen.
